title: A Former DOGE Operative Won a Federal Contract. Then Things Got Messy
gist: HHS awarded a $200,000 sole-source AI/modernization contract to Yat Choi LLC (GovMaxxing), owned by former DOGE/NDS-affiliated OPM contractor Yat Choi, four days after posting it; after small AI contractor CoA Solutions filed a GAO bid protest, HHS terminated the award and canceled the solicitation. A procurement law expert calls the sole-source justification 'thin' given 75 bids, and the piece notes other ex-DOGE members (Cathedral, Ethan Shaotran) are also positioning for federal contracts.

themes.theme: The HHS sole-source award and its reversal

insights.claim: HHS posted a $200,000 contract for 'modernization discovery, prototyping, and implementation-planning engagement' in September 2026 and awarded it sole-source four days later to Yat Choi LLC, owned by former DOGE and National Design Studio technologist Yat Choi.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Shows how informal networks from DOGE can translate into rapid, non-competitive federal IT/AI awards.
insights.locator: In September, the Department of Health and Human

insights.claim: HHS justified the sole-source award by saying conventional consulting firms would need to assemble a multidisciplinary team to cover business-process modernization, AI, automation, technical architecture and rapid prototyping.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Agencies favoring single generalist AI builders over traditional consultancies is a competitive threat to incumbent federal IT integrators.
insights.quote: conventional consulting firms generally would need to assemble a multidisciplinary team or obtain additional technical resources
insights.locator: The bid was for a project set to run

insights.claim: After CoA Solutions, a small government AI software firm that had bid below $200,000, filed a GAO bid protest in October, HHS terminated the award to Choi at no cost and canceled the solicitation, leading the GAO to dismiss the protest.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Bid protests remain an effective check on irregular awards, adding execution risk for politically connected contractors.
insights.quote: HHS voluntarily took corrective action, terminating the contract at no cost to the government and canceling the solicitation
insights.locator: According to CoA, in response to the bid protest

insights.claim: Procurement law expert Jessica Tillipman says 75 bids on the HHS contract indicate it was not a unique service, making the sole-source justification thin, since true single-source awards usually rest on a technical reason like non-interoperable tools or unique parts.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Provides a test for spotting fragile sole-source awards likely to be overturned on protest.
insights.quote: Usually, when there's only one responsible source, there's a technical reason

insights.claim: Tillipman argues Choi's work with DOGE and NDS across agencies could create the appearance of a conflict of interest even though he was never a regular federal employee, and that subcontractor conflicts can be imputed to prime contractors.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Conflict-of-interest exposure could follow ex-DOGE talent into primes that subcontract to them.
insights.quote: The whole thing is highly irregular overall.

insights.claim: Multiple former DOGE members are seeking federal contracts: Ethan Shaotran started a defense tech startup listed on the System for Award Management since April, and Jack Stein, Gavin Kliger, Luke Farritor and Marko Elez launched AI defense company Cathedral, listed since July.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A new cohort of politically connected AI/defense-tech startups is entering federal procurement, a competitive factor for govtech incumbents.
insights.locator: Choi is not the only former DOGE

insights.claim: None of the ex-DOGE startups have received prime federal contracts, but whether they work as subcontractors is unknown because subcontractor relationships are not publicly visible.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Subcontracting opacity means ex-DOGE firms' government revenue and the primes they partner with cannot be tracked publicly.

insights.claim: The National Design Studio, led by Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia and created after Elon Musk left government, has served as a landing pad for several DOGE members including Edward Coristine.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: NDS is a continuing channel for DOGE-style tech influence on federal IT after DOGE itself wound down.
insights.locator: Choi’s role in the US government

insights.claim: Choi, a Canadian citizen and US lawful permanent resident, worked on DOGE and NDS modernization as an OPM contractor rather than an employee, a structure that sidesteps rules generally barring foreigners from full-time or special government employee roles.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Contractor status is a loophole for staffing sensitive government modernization work, with governance implications.
insights.locator: Choi confirmed that he is a Canadian citizen

insights.claim: Choi announced on November 5, two days after Republicans lost the midterm elections, that he had left OPM and launched GovMaxxing to keep contracting with the government.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Midterm losses may push administration-linked technologists out of government and into contracting, shifting the govtech landscape.

insights.claim: Following a nationwide FAA flight grounding, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called for funding to modernize air traffic control, and Choi publicly pitched his company for the FAA's modernization efforts.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Air traffic control modernization is emerging as a funded federal IT priority that will attract contractors.
